faces.f: The earth walks, strongest of all.

"Wherever the strong would harm the weak, I will be there."
—Ajani Goldmane
"Humans bring nothing but suffering and deceit. They are not welcome in my forest."
Pharika has written her secrets on its bones so that only the worthy may discover them.
Whether hunter or hunted, Kathril chooses when it is seen.
Silent as a snowdrift. Inexorable as an avalanche.
It gathers against the coming storm.
"My heart beats with the rhythm of the forest."
Few who encounter the strange, human-like grove leave once the lilting chorus of the dryads reaches their ears.
The soldiers were hopelessly outmatched, having brought only swords, ballistas, fire, spellcraft, and several large cannons to the battle.

"Of course it will grow beyond control—it was designed to choose its own evolution."
—Momir Vig
"I never thought I'd spend my life fighting. I'm a maker, not a destroyer."
"Death tried to uncrown me. But now I return, king of a greater realm."
"The raging gale fans the flames of righteous wrath."
His enemies wondered if the lich king's brutal death and unnatural rebirth had been his plan all along.
Many sigils, one purpose.
The orcs believe Sek'Kuar still lives in the Karplusan Mountains, gathering his dead army, intent on revenge.
While Kaya is guildmaster, Teysa waits patiently at the center of the Orzhov web of power.
She talks using riddles her disciples alone can unravel.

"Many thought they knew its weakness. They are dead."
—Kelsien, the Plague

"Fuses? We have more than enough! Now . . . which one was it?"
—Flearan One-Eye, goblin engineer
By guild tradition, any puddle of multicolored light on the cobblestones can serve as neutral ground.

"The perfection of the lotus reminds me of my hopes for this world . . . and my failures. I will not rest until I've atoned for them."
—Karn
"Arise, great one, and cleanse the world of our enemies!"
Ghirapur's most celebrated inventors have been immortalized in clockwork.

"I've seen my share of baubles, minister. Whatever ostentatious bit of glitter you have there won't convince me to ... Oh my."
—Emperor Ayrelion
The blade glows only for Zendikar's chosen.
When they're done pummeling each other, the fighters relax companionably in the springs, warming their sore muscles.
The loudest and most heartfelt cheers come from the cheap seats.
Between matches, combatants practice to stay in peak mental and physical form.
To get to Valor's Reach, competitors must first make a name for themselves in the smaller arenas.
Where victors are commemorated and moments of glory immortalized.
Anyone who says love is the greatest gift of all has never received a ruby the size of their face.

"Dissent will become perfection."
—Elesh Norn

"Served cold? Nonsense! The best way to serve revenge is with an elephant of nervous disposition! Everyone knows that."
—Avenir the Petty
"I've heard enough from you, heretic."
Attacking a kami is considered bad luck, so seasoned mages have developed techniques to usher them back to the spirit realm without violence.
His heart is pure. His world is not.

"What's the big deal? All things will eventually cease to be, this one's just getting a head start."
—Edorin, the Timesmith
A good blacksmith will craft the weapon you ask for. A master will craft the weapon you dream of.
"Nice spell you got there. Be a shame if something happened to it."
"Does this choice really seem so simple, syr knight?"
One half-written novel, a year's worth of lecture notes, and several grocery lists later, Shiori began to wonder if she'd hacked the wrong terminal.
The luckiest acolytes were those who didn't survive long enough to see the archfiend's return.
"A small sip here and a small sip there, and all of a sudden I need a new dance partner."
As the ritual neared its climax, the exultant cultists waited with bated breath, unaware of the looming consequences of the scroll's translation error.
"Today will end with a feast," gloated the dragon. And what a feast it was.
Keep looking up and you'll miss what's right in front of your face.
"If they didn't want me to steal this, they should've used more than seven layers of shatterproof antimagus glass."
"Linear time? You may as well believe in triangular gravity!"
"First you summon the lightning, then you make it dance."

"Opposable thumbs, opposable toes, prehensile tails, boundary issues . . . no treasure is safe from a goblin."
—Captain Lannery Storm

"I hope the review board was paying attention, because my thesis would be hard to do twice."
—Spyracus, Prismari mage-student
"Captain, is now a good time to mention I'm allergic to spiders?"
"Just as new shoots rise from winter's slumber, so too will my people rise to greatness once again."

"The trees keep our history better than any digital device."
—Satsuki, the Living Lore

"Nonsense! Everyone knows that snakes are sluggish and docile when cold!"
—Bodrick the Overconfident, last words
Matic had only taken the ring to appease his grandmother when she'd pressed it insistently into his palm. As the rats scurried away from its light, he understood her urgency.
Those who crave power for selfish ends find that it always floats just beyond their fingertips, forever maddeningly out of reach.
Nothing shatters a peaceful life like newfound riches.

"The 'pinnacle' of advancement is a concept that exists only in the narrow minds of those with no ambition."
—Yawgmoth

"I'm not sure who's in charge around here, but I'm pretty sure I know where to go to find out."
—Corliss the Wanderer

"This garden is where my grandmother had her first breakthrough on biomodular logarithmic theory!"
—Zimone, Quandrix mage-student
At a certain point, the only thing a wizard wants for is time. And after that, nothing.

"It's almost as exciting as watching a great battle from the Blood Age in person!"
—Quintorius, Lorehold mage-student

"Sometimes you just need to be inspired by a massive explosion or a color that didn't exist five seconds ago."
—Rootha, Prismari mage-student

"Witherbloom always has the home-field advantage."
—Dina, Witherbloom mage-student

"Sure, true self-worth has to come from within, but trophies are nice too."
—Killian, Silverquill mage-student
"Leadership is both a blessing and a burden. Every day I strive to prove myself a worthy steward to those who follow me."
"The body has limits. The mind does not."
"I am the bridge between sea and sky. Wind and waves alike rise at my whim."
"Live an exemplary life. Die a worthy death. Rise in eternal glory."
"If you travel only to reach a destination, you will miss the point of the journey."
As wild and untamed as the Roil from which it was born.
"A life is meaningless until put to use."
Living proof that friendship and loyalty transcend language.
"As Yavimaya yearns to grow beyond its boundaries, so must we spend our lives seeking new horizons."
"Life and death are two sides of the same coin."
"I've survived a century's worth of assassination attempts, but this might be the most pathetic of them all."
All that glitters is yours.
"Mindless violence withers in the face of a master's skill."
"Anyone can make their audience beg for an encore . . . I prefer mine to beg for mercy!"
"Is the knowledge really forbidden because it is dangerous to you? Or perhaps because it is dangerous to those who seek to control you?"
An unwelcome light on a dark and foggy night.
"Come to slay the dragon for the good of the kingdom? How terribly predictable."

"Why should our fates be decided by pompous decrees from an empty throne? Fight with me and seize the reins of your own destiny!"
—Risona, leader of the Asari Uprisers
With a roar, the forest came alive.
"Be calm, wise spirit. You are in a world that is not your own, but I am not your enemy."

"Model? I'm insulted. It's by all reasonable metrics a fully functional planetary system, scaled down for easier study."
—Urza, to Tawnos
"All stories eventually come to an end."
Unburdened from mortality, archaics wander the Vastlands seeking knowledge only they can comprehend.
To the Zendikari, an apocalypse. To the Eldrazi, a day like any other.
And still the titans were not sated.

faces.chapters:
(As this Saga enters and after your draw step, add a lore counter. Sacrifice after III.)

faces.f: "We travel to know the land—its sacred spirit, its perils and blessings."

"It is possible that some queens are not born queens, but evolve into that form over time."
—Rukarumel, field notes

"The way it shakes its hood is astonishingly irritating."
—Neena, outland scout
They hunt on pure instinct, driven by the will of the hive mind with no time wasted on independent thought.
A single survivor can repopulate a devastated hive within a week.
Mirrodin's heart beats with Phyrexian oil.

"The emergence of the Eldrazi isn't necessarily a bad thing, as long as you've already lived a fulfilling and complete life without regrets."
—Javad Nasrin, Ondu relic hunter
The continent of Bala Ged was ravaged by massive Eldrazi of Ulamog's lineage, its lush jungles and cascading rivers reduced to dust.
It embodies all possible meanings of the word "infinite."
All will be harvested.
The Eldrazi hunger without limit and consume without pause.

"For those without the Planeswalker spark, the merest touch of the Blind Eternities can kill."
—Ugin
Dust and memory are all that remain in Ulamog's wake.

"It seems docile enough. Perhaps we could train it to reap the grain—it would be the easiest harvest season of our lives!"
—Georgina, farmer, now deceased
In their final moments, the demons gazed upon grace in its purest form.
Newborn slivers will sometimes wrap themselves playfully around a human's finger. They grow out of the "playful" part.
Gideon and Liliana may not have seen eye to eye, but that did not stop them from fighting side by side.
Few escape the Underworld. Fewer still escape fate.

"There is no greater burden than choosing who to save."
—Kamahl, druid acolyte

faces.f: "Scholars seek to understand the way the world is. I wish to shape the world into what it should be."
"For justice and peace, I will keep watch."
"My time will come, when every soul will bask in my glory and obey my law."
"It's us against the world. Forever."

"Nine hells! How does something with no eyes see so far?"
—Max, Benalish scout
When Asha left Bant, she ensured that the world would have protection and order in her absence.
As the muscle cords of the creature twitched, Hanna saw an unsettling unanimity in the others' rippling flesh. She didn't know what it meant, but she urged Sisay to keep the ship at a safe distance.
She formed a friendship with several playful spirits, and soon "the pack" was known as the source of much mischief in Eiganjo.
"The realm of the gods opens before me!"
The smallest seed of regret can bloom into redemption.
Centuries ago, one man's vengeance plunged the world into ice and darkness.
Its graceful glide paints the ocean floor with strokes of luminescence.
Its call disrupts the delicate balance of the inner ear, disorienting intruders without direct confrontation.
Oona's song is like a twisted dinner chime. All the faeries return home, but it is Oona who feasts—on the stolen dreams and rumors they serve her.
"Inform our allies in the Tenth and throw the circuit. It's about to get weird."

"The union of sea and sky makes a perfect cover."
—Talrand, sky summoner

"I wish we'd never visited that accursed hive. Even here, surrounded by nothing but clouds, I swear I can still hear the horrible clicking, slithering sounds."
—Monihan, aerial surveyor
"For the sake of the Multiverse, I will keep watch."
Once the last few slivers the Riptide Project controlled were dead, there was nothing to keep the island from being completely overrun.

"Species XR17 feeds upon the mental energies of its victims. This explains why the goblins remain unaffected."
—Riptide Project researcher
"Rich" is a relative term.

"Everything around here has cut a deal with gravity."
—Gerrard of the Weatherlight

"One would think I would be accustomed to unexpected returns."
—Hanna, *Weatherlight* navigator
Panic spread like wildfire as the demons of Immersturm poured into Bretagard, slaughtering as they came.

"Someone's been tampering with the graves again. But what kind of grave robber uses a pickax?"
—Morgan, cemetery groundskeeper
Crippling fear precedes it. A foul stench accompanies it. Death follows in its wake.

faces.chapters:
(As this Saga enters and after your draw step, add a lore counter. Sacrifice after III.)
I — Each opponent sacrifices a creature or planeswalker of their choice.
II — Each opponent discards a card.
III — Put target creature or planeswalker card from a graveyard onto the battlefield under your control.

faces.f: Harpies are among the most detested creatures in all of Theros... and they thoroughly deserve it.
The hive knows no fear or mercy, only hunger.

"A great many dangerous creatures call this region home. They all avoid the slivers."
—Foothill guide

"Holy places are no longer sanctuary from death, and death is no longer sanctuary from anything."
—Thalia, Knight-Cathar
Traveling across the desert alone, you might assume you'd see them coming, but that would be your third mistake.

As the time streams grew more and more unstable, Dominaria's creatures struggled to adapt. The intense pressures led to many dead ends but also to lethal new forms that appeared as suddenly as the ashen rains.
When it wriggled closer to a thrum of slivers, their talons hardened and glinted in the sun. One took a playful swipe at a tree trunk, and its new blade cut clean through.

"Brilliant! They evolved away from energy-taxing brains and respond only to spinal reflex arcs from the hive mind."
—Rukarumel, field journal
It's in the nature of fire to grow.

"The key to safely studying any sliver is to find out what provokes it, then absolutely never do that."
—Rukarumel, field journal
There is no such thing as surprising a sliver.
When a species becomes so dominant that no other can compete, evolution gets creative.
Her webs, spun from her own hair, reach from Nyx to the mortal world and even into the Underworld.

faces.chapters:
(As this Saga enters and after your draw step, add a lore counter. Sacrifice after III.)
I — Each player mills three cards.
II — Exile up to two target cards from graveyards. For each creature card exiled this way, you gain 1 life.
III — Return target creature or land card from your graveyard to your hand.

faces.f: Within weeks, more slivers nested in Otaria than ever existed on Rath.
All seeds share a common bond, calling to each other across infinity.

"Vine-wreathed, he nurtures life among the dead."
—Psemilla, Meletian poet
The emotional echoes of dryad gatherings attract lost souls.
"The wise learn from successes as well as mistakes."
"How truly vast this city must be, that I have traveled so far and seen so much, yet never once found the place where the buildings fail."
Drink deep, and know the path to the heart of the wilds.
Squee had been disemboweled many times before, but never by something so stunningly beautiful.
The kami permit few mortals to dwell in Jukai Forest, but the clever, playful tanuki are welcomed as friends and guardians.
The distinction of bearing the gods' banner is nothing compared to the glory of being closer to Nyx.
Their pearlescent scales are highly sought after by those who lack the instincts for self-preservation.
Slivers will swiftly adapt to fill any evolutionary niche, even if that niche is "earthshaking apex predator."

faces.chapters:
(As this Saga enters and after your draw step, add a lore counter. Sacrifice after III.)
I, II — Mill two cards, then you may return a creature card from your graveyard to your hand.
III — Return all land cards from your graveyard to the battlefield, then shuffle your graveyard into your library.

faces.f:
"The colossal thing rumbled over the ridge, tree husks crumbling before it. The ones we were already fighting howled as it came, their muscles suddenly surging, and we knew it was time to flee."
—Llanach, Skyshroud ranger
From the cracks in the stone, she reads stories of the past. From the swirling vines, she glimpses visions of the future.
"My time will come, when no road will divide the endless verdure of the trees."
The directors of the Riptide Project wanted instant results on the sliver experiments. They got their wish.
Nature grows solutions to its problems.
The arrival of spring's first flowers is a sacred occasion to Karametra's acolytes, who fill the Setessan woods with song in celebration.
Cantankerous and territorial, sandwurms claim even the skies above their dunes.
"A blessing is not a gift. It is a duty."
Those who love the woods only wish to spread its majesty.
The venom softens tissue and liquefies internal organs, allowing the slivers to feed freely without wasting time chewing.

"Graceful? Yes. Beautiful? Absolutely. Harmless? Definitely not."
—Fyndhorn elder

(As this Saga enters and after your draw step, add a lore counter. Sacrifice after III.)
I — Destroy target nonland permanent an opponent controls.
II — Search your library for a Forest card, put it onto the battlefield tapped, then shuffle.

faces.f: Forked tails rustled. Talons clicked. A lone sliver streaked overhead like jagged lightning, and the hive thundered.
Bred as living shields, these slivers have proven unruly—they know they cannot be caught.
"Your own frailty is your undoing. I am merely the one to expose it."
Anarchy comes in many forms: social, individual, Gruul . . .

"When establishing a new hive in hostile territory, slivers abandon all sense of individual self-preservation to ensure the queen's survival."
—Rukarumel, field journal

"Since the last sliver arrived, even our mightiest relics splinter into shards as soon as we bring them against the hive."
—Llanach, Skyshroud ranger
Mogglings have been known to play ball with hibernating slivers, completely unaware of their true nature.
He had heard rumors of the cities—the constant noise, the stagnant air, the tainted water—and he had no wish to learn if they were true.
Warm enough to incubate eggs or incinerate those who would eat them.
Even after a false god tore the magic from Dominaria, power still radiated from the Mirari sword that slew her.
Though Volrath is long dead, the slivers have become everything he wanted them to be: mindless instruments of destruction and despair.
"For the lost and forgotten, I will keep watch."
"The threads of magic that protect this place were woven by my will."

"This is the source, the line unbroken since the calamity that brought such monsters to our shores."
—Hastric, Thunian scout
"Through every verdant field, every bough that hangs heavy with fruit, Karametra shows her love."
It provides what every discerning mage requires—time to think.
The maze-like design embodies the core of Azorius law—strict structure designed to test wills and stall change.

"Have you ever held a Boros signet? There's a weight to it that belies its size—a weight of strength and of pride."
—Agrus Kos

"The Northern Beacon flared, and even before the drawbridge finished its descent, the knights charged out."
—*Legend of the Gilded Knights*
Only the Eldrazi mind thinks in the warped paths required to open the hedrons and tap the power within.
Guarded by cartographers, disdained by warlords, coveted by adventurers.

"We shall forever roam."
—Ayli, high priest of the Eternal Pilgrims

"You've begun to understand the hedrons' true purpose," said Ugin. "The Eldrazi can be imprisoned."
"And how did that work out last time?" asked Jace.
Before being presented to its lord, each shaku is blessed by every hero of every region within that lord's domain.
The Izzet signet is redesigned often, each time becoming closer to a vanity portrait of Niv-Mizzet.

"What is mana but possibility, an idea not yet given form?"
—Jhoira, master artificer
Most mirrors show your reflection. Others show your potential.
Nevinyrral's final act of spite was to make sure all of his magic was destroyed along with him.

"Through even our darkest days, we must never cease creating. Each new invention brings value to the world, be it beauty, utility, or both."
—Rashmi, aether-seer
The myr are like the Glimmervoid: blank canvases on which to build grand creations.
The spirit dragon Ugin arranged the hedrons of Zendikar to direct leylines of energy. To disrupt one is to unleash devastation and chaos.
Fields of battle turn to fields of grain.
Scholars say that arbiters exist on every world, created by an unknown hand to enforce justice.
Cast out of Garenbrig for his crimes, Ennor turned to fae magic to fashion the perfect weapon for his revenge.
The great library in the Museum of Old Capenna has a million volumes on display—and miles of passages hidden behind them.

"The sun banishes darkness every morning. I too will rise with such assuredness."
—Huatli

"Good ideas don't take time. They take a lot of bad ideas first."
—Ral Zarek
It is the forest beyond the horizon, the mountain waiting to be climbed, the new land across the endless sea.
Even a fragment of a powerstone contains within it not just energy, but space—vast dimensions trapped in fragile crystal.
There is a sanctuary that reveals itself only to those graced by the *eludha*—the mystical connection between bonder and monster.
The continent of Murasa lies beneath a blanket of dense vegetation, its enormous branches tangled so thickly that some inhabitants never see the ground.
Travelers bathe in the falls to wash away curses from the pucas who lurk nearby.
On the volcanic continent of Akoum, bizarre vegetation clusters around gas vents, and jagged mountain peaks rise high into the air.
Each temple is a door to a horrible future.

"It was a strange morning. When we awoke, we found our trees transformed. We didn't know whether to water them or polish them."
—Pulan, Bant orchardist
History is not delicately woven. It is hammered with fire.

"The most powerful dreams visit those who shelter in a dragon's skull."
—Chianul, Who Whispers Twice
A smoldering storm of chilling fire.
A seething locus of reverent rage.
All are welcome.
On Naya, ambition and treachery are scarce, hunted nearly to extinction by the awe owed to terrestrial gods.

"I can't protect everyone here. But those I can, I will."
—Karn
Sometimes the strongest weapon you can hold in your hand is another hand.
The gate of every kithkin doun is a cunning trap, intended to spill visitors into an oubliette from which there is no escape.
When asked how many paths reach enlightenment, the monk kicked a heap of sand. "Count," he smiled, "and then find more grains."
A hungry lair of flourishing rot.

"Only the weak imprison themselves behind walls. We live free under the wind, and our freedom makes us strong."
—Zurgo, khan of the Mardu
The dense jungle surrenders to a lush and lavish expanse. At its center uncoil the spires of Qarsi Palace.
The continent of Ondu is a vast plateau crisscrossed by deep trenches and meandering rivers.
Hobs bury their kin far from home. They believe the dry, open ground keeps hags from stealing the bones and gwyllions from stealing the spirits.
That which endures, survives.
Jund is a world as cruel as those who call it home. Their brutal struggles scar the land even as it carves them in its image, a vicious circle spiraling out of control.
When the last scrap of flesh is scoured away, the Curse of Wandering ends. Then the dead may sleep.
Once a center for knowledge, Sea Gate now serves as a reminder of what was lost.
For wisdom's sake, it was built high to gaze on all things. For glory's sake, it was built high as a testament of power. For strength's sake, it was built high to repel all attacks.
A flickering beacon of righteous corruption.
The gods known to the merfolk as Ula, Emeria, and Cosi were nothing more than false memories of a monstrous trinity: the Eldrazi titans Ulamog, Emrakul, and Kozilek.
Remote but always watching, the soaring city of Otawara moves over Kamigawa with a purpose that few understand.
The continent of Guul Draz is a geothermal swampland reeking of heat and decay.
On Otaria, peace and harmony are rare. Places that provide both are cherished.
On the continent of Tazeem, rushing waters plunge through narrow canyons into mist-cloaked lakes.

"When gods become apathetic, the people will worship anyone who answers their pleas."
—Kiora

"The voice calls me here, yet I see only bones. Is this more dragon trickery?"
—Sarkhan Vol
In his hunger for power and knowledge, Urza dug deep into Dominaria's ancient past.
Urza threw himself into his research, pushing the boundaries of both possibility and morality.
Urza studied the creations of the Thran not simply to learn from them, but to surpass them.
A figure is moved on a map, and the tide of war changes.
"Live an exemplary life. Die a worthy death. Rise in eternal glory."
*Strixhaven Star* food critic Aspen Van Gnoot's coverage of the fight would go on to win a student journalism award for outstanding war reporting.
It is everything and nothing.
She sings for all those who have been silenced.
"Zendikar will triumph this day, and our armies will fly with angels."
Light streaked down from the heavens, and a voice whispered in the soldier's ear: "You shall not fall today."
"With the right tools, even the sky is within reach."

"Who among you has the courage to face certain death? Who will heed my call?"
—Rayel Vanger, Firstblade of Thune
A righteous sovereign makes for a blessed realm.
"The Boros fight for justice. The Azorius fight for law. I hold the line between, and make sure the people are given both."

"I find its symmetry pleasing. It rids our world of offensive refuse while disposing of itself."
—Dolomarus, Proctor of the Clean
He vowed he would never rest until he reached his destination. He doesn't know how right he was.
His prowess gives the guildless hope that they can hold out against tyranny.

"There's never a good time for a disaster or an attack. That's why we're here."
—Oren, militia captain

"This is about more than aether or inventions. Tezzeret's schemes must be stopped!"
—Ajani Goldmane
In life, they were a motley crew: farmers, lords, cutpurses, priests. In death, they are united in singular, benevolent purpose.
Beneath the gaze of angels, only the righteous may stand without fear.
She chooses her riders carefully and bears them to glory in battle after battle.
Kor have no concept of exploration. They return to homelands forgotten.
For a moment they stood tall, all fear forgotten.
The Consulate keeps watch at each of the eleven bridges to ensure that the market remains a haven for commerce, not for con artists.
"Once Avacyn returned, I hoped I'd never need these things again. I didn't think I'd be dusting them off to use against angels."
The Orzhov care not for repentance, only repayment.

"One who ruled willing subjects would need no such protection."
—Adriana, Captain of the Guard
"Bant's most gallant knights wear my sigil, and for that I am humbled."
Death can wait.
Like blinking or breathing, responding to an alarm is an involuntary reflex.

"She sees beyond technology to what it enables."
—Glacian, powerstone engineer
Some timelines forever fray, branch, and intermingle. Others end abruptly.
She parts the clouds so sunlight can reach even the darkest lairs and duskiest tombs.
Light as a feather. Sharp as an angel's wrath.
In the moment of truth, it is as though time stands still, and the whale waits, suspended in the sky.
The generals each surveyed their devastated forces. Then, slowly, they turned to each other and raised their swords.

"Cut the beasts out from under them and their strength is nothing."
—Vona of Iedo, Butcher of Magan
Instinctively drawn to the light of its "mother-sun," each slith follows that sun's path around Mirrodin.
The strength of the one is the strength of the many.
In a flash of light and a burst of aether, despair turned to hope and defeat turned to victory.

"Margaret has traveled with me to the end of the world and back."
—Hewen Frit, merchant

"I prefer loyalty to be a matter of respect, not of magic. But one does what one must."
—Kaalia of the Vast

"Your concern for my safety is touching, but as long as your gunners remain reliably erratic, I see no reason to change course."
—Admiral Yelise, to Commodore Axurik
Jace tumbled down the waterfall and plunged deep into his past.

"I don't understand why he works so hard on a device to duplicate a sound so easily made with hand and armpit."
—Barrin, progress report
A throne built on wisdom cannot be toppled.
"They'll never see me coming."
"Garl, adjust the slurry dispensers. Garl, fetch more corpses. Garl, quit crying and give me your brain tissue. If he doesn't stop being so rude, I'm quitting."
"There's no better place to divine the future than at a nexus of branching presents."
Strong wings make strong winds.

"His energy is as boundless as the powerstones'."
—Rebbec, architect of ascension
"I don't need a map to find riches."
"Why perch in the crow's nest when I can fly like the crows?"

"Many hands make light work."
—Ludevic, necro-alchemist
Enthusiasm is no match for preparation.
"Tell you what, you keep the rope."
Past, present, and future surged through the wizard's mind, bringing a flood of possibilities.
Her prophecies amaze her even as she speaks them.
